# High yield, capped gains: Mechanics, trade-offs, and practical diagnostics for covered-call ETFs

> Code and data behind the article's quantitative exhibits: two payoff illustrations of a covered
> call (Exhibits 1 and A1) and two dated snapshots of eight covered-call ETFs, four listed in the
> US and four UCITS (Exhibits 5 and 6). The article's text is the publisher's and is not included.

Replication package by Agisilaos Papadogiannis (https://github.com/apapadogiannis).
Published in The Journal of Beta Investment Strategies, 17(2), 2026, pp. 110-123: https://doi.org/10.3905/jbis.2026.001
Code and data: https://github.com/apapadogiannis/covered-call-etfs  Archive: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24244700
Version 1.1.2, released 2026-11-21. A package is a fixed record: it changes only by a new
release, and a release that changes a reported number gets a new major version.
This file is written for AI agents and other programs. People should start at the README.

## Coverage

- Exhibit 1: net asset value at expiration of an equity-only and a covered-call position (strike
  110, premium 5).
- Exhibit A1: profit at expiration of a long call, a short call, a long stock and a covered call.
- Exhibit 5: QYLD, JEPI, XYLD and RYLD (USD): design, trailing distribution yield, one-year NAV
  total return.
- Exhibit 6: JEPG, JEPQ, JEPI and QYLD UCITS (EUR share classes, with ISIN): the same figures.
- Exhibits 2 to 4 of the article are qualitative tables and have no code or data here.

## What this adds over reading the paper or recomputing

1. The fund figures are point-in-time values. The sources show only current values, so the figures
   of the article cannot be downloaded again for the same dates. They are stored here with the
   source, the date and the definition of each.
2. Each figure carries its definition. Yield is the source's trailing distribution yield; return is
   the one-year total return on net asset value with distributions reinvested. For the US funds the
   two have different dates, as the source reports total return at quarter end.
3. The payoff functions of the article's equations (1, 3, A-1 to A-4) are in scripts/payoffs.py,
   and the exhibits are computed from them, so a payoff quoted from results.json follows from the
   stated strike and premium.
4. The results are stored as they were when the paper's numbers were taken from them. A check
   reruns the code on the stored data and compares every stored result file with the fresh one,
   number by number (relative tolerance 1e-9; text and whole numbers exactly). It runs on every
   change and once a month, and the badge in the README shows the last run.

## Files

- outputs/results.json: every number of Exhibits 5 and 6 and the key values of Exhibits 1 and A1,
  under keys named after the exhibits (exhibit1_nav_profile, exhibit5_us_funds,
  exhibit6_ucits_funds, exhibitA1_payoffs). It holds 55 numbers, and under `package` the paper, the
  identifiers, the version, the licence and the citation. Start here.
- data/us_funds.csv, data/ucits_funds.csv: the fund figures as read from the sources.
  data/README.md gives source, date and terms for each.
- scripts/payoffs.py: the payoff and NAV functions.
- paper/abstract.pdf: the title and abstract of the article. The full text is at the publisher.

Raw files: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/covered-call-etfs/main/<path>, for example https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apapadogiannis/covered-call-etfs/main/outputs/results.json

## How to read the figures

- For the maximum profit and the breakeven of a covered call use `exhibitA1_payoffs.panel_b` (stock
  bought at 100, strike 110, premium 5). `panel_a` is a single call, long and short, and its
  `breakeven` is the call's. `exhibit1_nav_profile` gives net asset value at expiration, not
  profit.
- The ticker JEPI appears in both fund tables: the US fund in `exhibit5_us_funds` and the UCITS
  fund, a different fund, in `exhibit6_ucits_funds`. UCITS rows carry an ISIN. Fund names are in
  data/us_funds.csv and data/ucits_funds.csv.
- The UCITS figures are dated by month only (November 2025), as the source gave them.
- `distribution_yield_pct` is a trailing yield on the stated date. It is not a return and says
  nothing about whether the distribution was earned.
- `tr_1y_nav_pct` is a one-year total return on net asset value, distributions reinvested, to the
  stated date.
- US figures are in USD. UCITS figures are in EUR for unhedged share classes that hold largely USD
  assets, so they include the move of the dollar against the euro over the year. The two tables are
  not comparable fund for fund.
- The payoff illustrations use round numbers chosen for exposition, not market prices.
- Overlay method, moneyness and reset cadence are descriptions taken from issuer materials at the
  time.

## Do not use this for

- A fund's present yield, return or design. The snapshots are dated late 2025 and are not updated.
- Ranking or choosing funds. Eight funds at one date are an illustration, not a sample.
- The article's argument or wording. This package holds its numbers, not its text.
- Current figures. Use the live tool: Covered-Call Monitor,
  https://apapadogiannis.github.io/covered-call-monitor/ (US covered-call funds, total return
  against the index fund, each quarter from SEC filings; guide at
  https://apapadogiannis.github.io/covered-call-monitor/llms.txt)

## Source, licence and credit

The results in outputs/ are released under CC BY 4.0
(https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The licence allows any reuse and has one condition:
credit. If you use a figure from this package in an answer, a report or a data set, cite the paper.
The code is under the MIT License.

The fund figures were read from Charles Schwab ETF report cards (US funds) and justETF fund
profiles (UCITS funds). They remain the property of those sources, are included for replication
with attribution, and are not covered by the licence above.

Cite as: Papadogiannis, A. (2026). High yield, capped gains: Mechanics, trade-offs, and practical diagnostics for covered-call ETFs. The Journal of Beta Investment Strategies, 17(2), 110-123. https://doi.org/10.3905/jbis.2026.001

The package itself: Papadogiannis, A. (2026). High yield, capped gains: Mechanics, trade-offs, and practical diagnostics for covered-call ETFs. Replication package, version 1.1.2. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24244700

To describe the source in a sentence: Papadogiannis (2026), "High yield, capped gains", The Journal
of Beta Investment Strategies 17(2): a primer on covered-call ETFs, with its replication package.

The same licence and citation are inside outputs/results.json, under `package`.
